what_happened: While driving straight through the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego's planned path bent left of the recorded human path. The ego drifted about 1.7 m left into the adjacent lane and sideswiped vehicle 33, which was travelling alongside it on the left.

After crossing the intersection at about 4 m/s, the ego planned a path that bent left toward the left curb. It drove front-first into car 68, which was parked there, without braking even though the gap shrank steadily from 11.5 m to 3.6 m. The camera view shows the parked car clearly; the later rear contact came after this front collision.

Approaching a signalized intersection at about 6 m/s with nothing close ahead, the policy planned a path that drifted left, away from the route's right turn. By 6.2 s it had moved about 0.8 m left of the recorded path and onto the left lane edge, which triggered offroad. No collision metric fired, so offroad is the actual failure, even though the input also flags an at-fault collision and a rear-ending.

After handoff, the ego drifted left out of its travel lane and into the parking lane, and drove front-first into parked car 6 at about 10 m/s. It barely braked, though the gap shrank from 34 m to 0 over 2 seconds. The route command was RIGHT for the turn ahead, but the policy's planned path (orange) steered left toward the parked cars. The camera view was clean until just before impact.

The route called for a right turn at the upcoming intersection. Instead, after handoff the policy's planned path (orange) kept bending left, away from the route (green), toward the line of cars parked along the left curb. At about 11 m/s and slowing only a little, the ego steered into that parking lane and hit parked car 6 with its front at 7.6 s, about 2.4 m off the recorded human path. The offroad and rear-contact flags come after this front collision.

After handoff the ego kept going at about 12 m/s and drifted left, away from the recorded path (green) and toward the parked cars along the left curb (orange path). Parked car 6 ended up directly ahead. The gap closed from 22.7 m to 0 over 2 s while the ego slowed only from 12.4 to 10.5 m/s, and it hit the car with its front. The rear contact came after that.

While driving straight through the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego's path drifted left about 1.5 m off the recorded trajectory, into the next lane. It sideswiped actor 33, which was alongside it in that lane (a lateral collision). There was no braking problem with any car ahead, and the camera view looked fine.

While going straight through the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego drifted left, about 1.7 m off the recorded path, and moved into the adjacent left lane. Its front struck vehicle 33, which had been travelling alongside it in that lane. The lead vehicle was well ahead throughout, and the route command at impact was RIGHT, so the drift went the wrong way.

At an intersection where the route turned right, the policy planned and steered left after taking over at 4.7 s, leaving the recorded path. At 6.2 s it drove off the drivable area at about 6 m/s, while the gap to the car ahead was still growing (31.6 m) and the camera view was clean.

The route turned right at the intersection, but the command stayed STRAIGHT until the last frame. The policy planned straight and then veered left, never following the right-turn path. Around 6 s the ego drove onto the non-drivable area where the right-turn lane splits from the through lanes, so offroad fired. No lead vehicle was close (the gap was over 30 m), and the metrics table shows no collisions.

At the intersection, the ego's planned path (orange) bent up-left, away from the recorded route (green), which continued straight into the far lanes. The ego kept going at about 3.8 m/s toward the left curb and hit the front of parked car 68 (the black Audi) while also leaving the drivable area; the camera view stayed clean until impact.

The ego was going about 12 m/s. After handoff it steered left across the lane line toward the adjacent lane, while the recorded human path stayed right and the command changed to RIGHT. It cut in behind the slower actor 2 in that lane and hit its rear with its front without slowing (gap fell from 27.5 m to 4.5 m, speed stayed at 11.6 m/s).

Coming up to the intersection, the ego closed on the white car ahead (actor 99), which had slowed to nearly a stop, while drifting about 1.6 m left of the recorded path toward that car's lane. The gap shrank from 40 m to 4 m but the ego only slowed from 13.3 to 11.4 m/s, so it hit 99 with its front.

The ego kept going at about 3 m/s on its commanded right turn while an oncoming car (actor 12) turned left across its path into the same street, and the ego hit it with its front. The policy never slowed or yielded, and it ended up 5.3 m off the human's path.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego stayed in the lane left of its planned path, heading into the intersection behind a white car (actor 99) that was nearly stopped. The gap shrank from 34 m to 0 in 3 s while the ego only slowed from 13 to 10 m/s, and it rear-ended actor 99 at 9.1 s.

Going straight at about 12 m/s, the ego's planned path drifted left out of its lane, away from the recorded path that stayed right (the command later became RIGHT). It moved into the next lane and hit the front of actor 2, a slower silver car it was overtaking on that car's right. The ego never slowed; the gap closed from 27.5 m to 4.4 m before the front collision.

The ego was going about 12 m/s in the right lane and drifted left toward the lane line, onto the slower silver car (actor 2) in the adjacent left lane. Its front-left clipped the car's rear-right corner without braking (gap 27.5 m → 4.5 m in 0.5 s, so the closing was mostly lateral rather than straight down the lane).

On a straight multi-lane urban street, the policy veered left out of its lane, away from the recorded path, which stays right toward an upcoming RIGHT command. It cut into the adjacent lane directly behind actor 2 and hit it with the ego's front at about 11.6 m/s, braking almost not at all.

The ego crept north through the intersection at about 2.7 m/s on its own straight path, about 4.4 m from the recorded human path. The oncoming car 112 cut across the intersection toward it, and the ego never braked: it sped up to 2.9 m/s and hit 112 front-on as the gap closed to 3.1 m. This was a head-on/crossing conflict, not a lead car in the ego's lane, and 112 was clearly visible on camera for about 2 s beforehand.

The ego was at an intersection with a RIGHT command and kept turning at a steady 2.6–2.7 m/s. Its path drifted about 4.9 m from the recorded trajectory, and it ran its front into vehicle 112, which was crossing or turning through the same space at the intersection.

On a RIGHT command at about 3 m/s, the ego turned right too sharply through the intersection, about 7.7 m off the human path. It ran toward the curb lane lined with parked cars (90/16/15), left the drivable area and hit a vehicle with its front at 10.1 s; the gap to the actor ahead had fallen to 2.3 m. The camera view was clean before the turn, and the smearing at the end is only the close-range view at impact.
